question: For the nonzero numbers \(a,\) \(b,\) and \(c,\) define \[(a,b,c)=\dfrac{a}{b}+\dfrac{b}{c}+\dfrac{c}{a}.\] Find \((2,12,9).\)
solution:
The definition tells us to substitute \(a=2\), \(b=12\), and \(c=9\), in that order. These numbers are all nonzero, so every fraction is defined. Simplifying and using the common denominator \(6\), we get
\[
\begin{aligned}
(2,12,9)&=\frac{2}{12}+\frac{12}{9}+\frac{9}{2}\\
&=\frac16+\frac43+\frac92\\
&=\frac{1+8+27}{6}=6.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus the answer is \(\boxed{6}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).

The criteria expressly find common factors and reduce until numerator and denominator are coprime. These are the common-factor contents of the endpoint; finding the greatest factor in a single step is only a shortcut and is outside this required scope.

edges.scope: dividing numerator and denominator by a common number

edges.reason: Once denominators agree, the target adds or subtracts numerators in equal fractional units, directly using same-denominator arithmetic.
